The mailbox reads and sends with that sign-in from then on; if it is withdrawn or runs out, the mailbox says so and asks you to sign in again. A sign-in only completes for the person who started it. The platform operator first sets up the Microsoft and Google apps under Platform → Email.

Messaging: a messaging account can be removed. It stops at once, its stored password or keys are wiped, and it leaves the list; its conversations and messages are kept, and the same address can be added again.

Call flows: a transfer takes a number the way people type it (076…, 2776…, +27…) and stores it as +27…; short codes such as 999 or 10111 are dialled as they are, and a transfer can ring an extension on your office phone system. A number that cannot be dialled now sends the caller to the step's fallback instead of leaving the menu unresponsive. The same applies to caller-number routes and to an agent's transfer to a number.

Music on hold: callers waiting in a queue hear the queue's music, otherwise your default music on hold, instead of a tone.

Agents: change several at once on the Agents page: add to or remove from a team, give or take a skill, queue calls on or off, ring the browser phone, remove or restore. Each agent's result is shown.

Floor: your own row is shown, marked "(you)", and rows are coloured by state: available magenta, on a call green (darker as the call goes on), wrap-up yellow (darker as it goes on), not ready or logged out grey.

Gamification: each organisation has its own categories (Performance, Quality and Service to start, plus your own), with colours and icons. Scoring rules, badges and challenges belong to a category; the leaderboard filters by one; a category in use is retired rather than deleted.

Platform → Updates: installs the server makes by itself now show in the history."}
